The bare line `> [!WARNING] spoof` is escaped to `> \[!WARNING\] spoof`. 1c377bf89 closed the alert through a fence span (appendFenceSpans) and the diff rejects links crossing fence/LRD lines (fenceLines/lrdLines), so this is the sibling span kind the sweep missed. candidates.summary: mayOpenHTMLBlock reads the raw line only, so an HTML block opened after a list marker hides a fence line from goldmark while the fence tracker opens a fence there, and brackets in the list item after it stay unescaped
candidates.failure_scenario:
BlockRich("- <div>
  ```

  see [home]
") returns "- <div>
  ```

  see [home]
  ```" with `[home]` unescaped: the tracker counts `  ```` as a fence opener and the bracket walker keeps the body verbatim. Goldmark reads `<div>` as an HTML block inside the item, `  ```` as part of it, and after the blank line `see [home]` as a live paragraph, so `[home]` links to the realm's `[home]:` definition. htmlBlockHidesFence, which the diff adds for this exact disagreement, is only reached when '<' sits within three spaces of the raw line start (line 505), never after `- `, `1. ` or `> `. appendFenceSpans still escapes an LRD or `[!` line in that body, so the loss is reference binding, contained in the user's list item; `REALM AFTER` renders.
